terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to scan the channels and write the night's log.

tasks.title: Back to the team's channel
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `radio_desk.py`, write a function called `scan` that takes the radio, a dictionary with the channel it is on, and a list of channels. It tunes the radio to each channel in turn, by changing `"channel"` in the radio itself, and calls `listen` with the radio there. It gives back a list of what `listen` gave back for each channel, in order. Afterwards the radio is on the channel it was on before, whatever happens: also when `listen` stops with an error on a channel it cannot tune to. That error must still reach the caller. Print what it gives back for `radio` and `[1, 2]`, then the channel the radio is on.

Check gives your file its own `listen`, calls `scan` with radios and channels of its own, a channel `listen` cannot tune to among them, and looks at what it gives back or the error that reaches Check, and at the channel the radio is on afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on finally.
Keep the channel the radio is on in a name, before anything changes.
Tune and listen in a loop inside a try.
Put the channel back in a finally block, and give back the list after it.
hints: A line after the loop never runs when `listen` stops with an error in the middle, so the radio stays on the last channel tried.
The lines under `finally:` run when the `try` ends well and when it stops with an error, and then the error carries on to the caller. Do not catch it, and do not return from inside `finally`.
The shape is `before = radio["channel"]`, then `try:` with the loop, then `finally:` with `radio["channel"] = before`, then `return` the list.

tasks.title: Close the log, whatever happens
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, Ailsa's `write_log` takes the path of a file, as text, and a list of entries, and writes the line `entry_line` gives for each entry into the file, in order. It opens the file with `open` and closes it at the end, so when `entry_line` stops with an error, the file is never closed. Change `write_log` so that the file is closed whatever happens, and an error from `entry_line` still reaches the caller. It still writes with `encoding="utf-8"`.

Check gives your file its own `entry_line`, calls `write_log` with files and entries of its own, entries with a time that is not written like `21:05` among them, and looks at what each file holds, at whether the file was left open, and at the error that reaches Check.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on what with does when something fails.
Look at when the close line runs, and when it does not.
Open the file on a with line instead, with the loop moved in under it.
hints: When `entry_line` stops, Python leaves `write_log` at that line: the lines after it, the close line among them, never run.
A file opened on a `with` line is closed as soon as the lines moved in under it end, even when one of them stops with an error. The error then carries on to the caller.
The shape is `with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as log:` with the `for` loop and its `log.write(entry_line(entry))` moved in under it.

tasks.title: All of the log, or none of it
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, write a function called `save_log` that takes the path of a file, as text, and a list of entries, and makes the file hold the line `entry_line` gives for each entry, in order, and nothing else. When `entry_line` stops with an error, the file must hold exactly what it held before, or not be there at all if it was not there before, and the error must still reach the caller. Write it with `encoding="utf-8"`; a `with` line closes it for you. Call it for `"saved.txt"` and `entries`.

Check gives your file its own `entry_line`, calls `save_log` with files and entries of its own, entries with a bad time among them, and looks at what each file holds afterwards, or whether it is there, and at the error that reaches Check.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on a partly written file.
Make the line of every entry first, into a list, before any file is opened.
Only then open the file for writing, and write the lines.
Try it with an entry whose time is wrong, and look at saved.txt.
hints: Opening a file with `"w"` empties it at once. If an entry stops with an error after that, the old log is gone and the new one is half written.
If every line is made before the file is opened, an error stops the function before the file is touched.
The shape is a loop that adds `entry_line(entry)` to a list, then `with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as log:` and `log.write("".join(lines))` under it.
